questions.q: What is the safe rollout order for setting `PasswordAuthentication no` on hru-web01 and hru-db01?
options: Edit sshd_config and restart sshd immediately from the only open session
Confirm key-based login works from a second, still-open session, run `sshd -t`, restart sshd, then verify a brand-new session works before closing the originals
Disable fail2ban first, then change the SSH config
Change the SSH port before touching password authentication
questions.explain: Restarting sshd from the only open session without a verified second connection is the single most common way to get locked out of a remote Linux server — this order avoids that.

questions.q: Why does `AllowUsers mvoss dgranger deploy` matter even though SSH already uses key-based authentication?
options: It replaces the need for keys entirely
It's an explicit allow-list checked after authentication, so even an account with a valid key is rejected if it isn't named
It only affects password authentication, not keys
It automatically rotates SSH keys
questions.explain: AllowUsers is a hard backstop on top of key-based auth — only the named accounts may connect at all, regardless of whether they hold a valid key.

questions.q: Why does fail2ban stay enabled on both servers even after PasswordAuthentication is set to no?
options: fail2ban has nothing left to do once keys are required
Defense in depth: a future misconfiguration could re-enable password auth, and fail2ban also catches connection floods and failed key attempts that clutter logs
fail2ban is required for ufw to function
fail2ban replaces the need for AllowUsers
questions.explain: fail2ban is a backstop against both future misconfiguration and ongoing noise from failed attempts, not something made redundant by key-only SSH.

questions.q: Why does hru-web01 get unattended-upgrades specifically called out as important, more than an internal-only server might?
options: Because it runs a different Linux distribution
Because it sits directly on the internet, making it the server most likely to actually face exploitation of a known, unpatched vulnerability if patching lags
Because unattended-upgrades only works on internet-facing servers
Because hru-db01 doesn't support automatic updates
questions.explain: An internet-facing host is exposed to opportunistic exploitation the moment a vulnerability becomes public, which is exactly why automatic patching matters most there.

questions.q: Why is hru-db01's ufw rule for its database port scoped to `10.20.5.11` specifically, rather than the whole internal subnet?
options: Because ufw doesn't support subnet ranges
Because hru-db01 should only ever be reachable from hru-web01, the one server that legitimately needs it, not from every host on the internal network
Because 10.20.5.11 is the database server's own address
Because the whole subnet is already blocked by default
questions.explain: Scoping to the exact IP of the one server that needs access (hru-web01) is tighter and more defensible than opening the port to an entire subnet.
